statement: Kernel-checked with advisory coverage pending. For every natural predicate A and cutoff N, the absolute difference between CodeMassTransport.mass A N and twice logMass A N is at most 6, from the positive-integer bound |weight(n)-2/n|<=6*(1/n-1/(n+1)). For every backward-closed A and real t, (33/100)*fullMass A(3*t/4-4)<=sourceMass A oeGuard(cutoff t)+2*C0+8, with C0=logMass(True,10^36)+2100*eps(10^36)/(1/1000)^2. This actual OE bound has no additional analytic hypothesis: the existing poor-fibre theorem, disjoint fibres, and n^3<(m+1)^4 prove the reciprocal production and physical source cutoff. The analytic threshold 10^36 is not a computational verification floor. OOEEProductionBound A means the eventual actual OOEE inequality with coefficient 11/100 at target cutoff 9*t/16-4 and a bounded nonnegative additive loss. It now suffices by itself for OddProductionBounds A. For a backward-closed A with a positive member it consequently gives reciprocal growth at exponent 5/8; for the failure class it and an eventual dyadic odd-failure rate e>3/8 imply termination. The OOEE production estimate and actual failure-rate bound remain explicit hypotheses and are not proved here.

Kernel-checked, advisory coverage pending. Exact target-fibre geometry, poor-target inclusion, reciprocal tail, physical cutoffs and OOEEProductionBound are not supplied.

Kernel-checked original OOEE mixed-mode cancellation; advisory statement coverage pending. Define M(x)=floor(x^(3/2)), Y(x)=M(x)^(3/2), and f_(i,j,k)(x)=(i/2)*x^(3/2)+(j/2)*Y(x)+(k/2)*x^(9/8). For every fixed integer triple with i nonzero or j nonzero and every fixed real L>=0, there exist B>0 and P0 such that, for every real P>=P0, real a and natural N with P<=a, a+2N<=2P and N<=L*P^(7/16), norm(sum_(n<N) e(f_(i,j,k)(a+2n))) <= B*P^(13/32). One B,P0 works for any fixed finite set of such triples. A second theorem requires only the actual N sample points to lie in [P,2P]; it removes and restores the last sample and increases the constant by one. The actual first-floor remainder is between zero and x^(-3/4) for x>0; for u=j/2 the summed original-to-retained phase comparison costs at most 10*pi*abs(u)*L*P^(1/4). Exact-overlap finite differencing, both coefficient signs, empty and short sums, and the smooth j=0,i-nonzero case are proved. There is no assumed cancellation, correlation or equidistribution input. Pure slow modes, frequency cutoffs growing with P, joint discrepancy, poor-target inclusion and physical production cutoffs are outside this statement. OOEEProductionBound and the actual failure-rate estimate remain open.

Kernel-checked, advisory coverage pending. Put M(x)=floor(x^(3/2)), Y(x)=M(x)^(3/2), V(x)=floor(Y(x)), W(x)=sqrt(V(x)). For x>=1, 0<=x^(9/8)-W(x)<=3*x^(-3/8). For P>=1, a>=P, L>=0 and N<=L*P^(7/16), replacing (w/2)*x^(9/8) by (w/2)*W(x) in the phase u*Y(x)+(v/2)*x^(3/2)+(w/2)*x^(9/8) changes its sum over x=a+2*n, n<N, by at most 3*pi*abs(w)*L*P^(1/16). Every fixed finite family of integer modes (i,j,k) with i or j nonzero therefore retains a common eventual O(P^(13/32)) bound for the actual phase (i/2)*x^(3/2)+(j/2)*Y(x)+(k/2)*W(x), when its samples lie in [P,2P] and N<=L*P^(7/16). Boundaries and empty sums are included; growing frequency sets and pure slow modes are excluded.

Kernel-checked actual OOEE production; advisory statement coverage pending. Using FateOOEEAssembly.fullMass, sourceMass, cutoff(t)=floor(exp(t)), and the actual ooeeGuard, there exists one real C>=0 such that for every natural predicate A closed under actual Juggler preimages and every real t, (11/100)*fullMass A(9*t/16-4)<=sourceMass A ooeeGuard(cutoff t)+C. The constant is independent of A and t. With eta=1/10000 and m>=10^9, a target outside CountPoor eta has at least (1107/10000)*m^(7/9) actual OOEE sources and reciprocal fibre mass at least 11/(100m). The proved summable count-poor tail bounds the discarded target mass uniformly. Exact fourth iterates give disjoint fibres, backward closure places their sources in A, and n<=2*m^(16/9) gives the physical cutoff. The established uniform mass-to-reciprocal comparison completes conserved-weight production. OOEEProductionBound is therefore discharged without an analytic hypothesis. The threshold 10^9 is an analytic size bound and does not change the computational verification floor.

For P>=1, u>0, 1<=h<=P^(1/16), P^(15/16)>=1024, abs(v)+abs(w)<=u*P^(3/4)/1024, 0<=eps<=1, and x in [P,2P] with G<=(x+2h)^(3/2)-x^(3/2)<=G+1, Lean proves -2*u*h*P^(-3/4)<=F_second(x)<=-u*h*P^(-3/4)/16. If G is an integer, N is natural, [a,a+2N] is contained in [P,2P], and the same carry inequalities hold throughout that closed interval, the spacing-two exponential sum has norm at most 256*N*sqrt(u*h*P^(-3/4)/16)+4/sqrt(u*h*P^(-3/4)/16). For L>=0 and N<=L*P^(7/16), this is at most (64*L*sqrt(u)+16/sqrt(u))*P^(3/8). The explicit size conditions hold eventually for fixed u,v,w, uniformly in h and the cell. Both derivatives, the vanishing constant and first-order anchor-curvature terms, the actual floor-to-cell implication, and error dominance are proved. The closed support retains the final increment. No weighted carry correlation, Fourier remainder, finite discrepancy, OOEE production, improved unconditional contagion, or termination theorem is asserted.

AI-assisted written analytic proof, pending independent mathematical review and analytic Lean verification. Let O(n)=floor(n^(3/2)), Q(n)=floor(sqrt(n)), e(n)=n+(n mod 2), and w(n)=log((e(n)+1)/(e(n)-1)). Let F_m consist of positive n with n and O(n) odd, O^2(n) and Q(O^2(n)) even, and Q^2(O^2(n))=m. Set W_m=sum_(n in F_m) w(n) and R_m=W_m/w(m). For every fixed 0<eta<1/9, sum_(m>=U, R_m<1/9-eta) 1/m is O_eta(U^(-7/9)) for all U>=1. For sufficiently large m, every fixed absolute deviation of R_m from 1/9 lies in a fixed finite union of resonance sets ||q*(9/8)*m^(2/9)||<=C_eta*m^(-7/9). Consequently, uniformly for arbitrary positive-integer target sets A and finite cutoffs X, sum_(m in A, m<=X) W_m >= (1/9-eta)*sum_(m in A, m<=X) w(m)-C'_eta. All four actual parity guards are retained. The proof is in juggler_ooee_poor_fibre_tail_note.md; the finite tests check inversion and guards only. No uniform per-target positivity, revised contagion exponent, or termination theorem is asserted.
